$GRAB & $GOTO connecting the Dots 🧵

TLDR: $GRAB valuation is way too cheap, and $GOTO will go away with or without this acquisition. And this is going to be a long thread, so be prepared, or you may want to skip this.

I have talked about this for months since Feb 2025 where I initiated a position in GRAB after my SEA vacation in multiple regions. I started to look into valuation, the history of the company, and how it was able to win 75% market share from many govt/state sponsored companies. In this thread I want to focus on how $GRAB would have gone 90-95% market share without $GOTO, and the history of it. And of course the Key enabler was Nadiem, now currently being prosecuted for how he relaxed IPO regulation, got unlimited funding from Indo State owned companies and Google, one of the largest company in the world. And somehow, this Tiny startup led by @AnthonyPY_Tan managed to win and now about to acquire $GOTO Mobility/Delivery for $1.5B(not its Fin Arm). 

1. Background

Nadiem Makarim (Gojek co-founder) stepped down as CEO in 2019 to become Indonesia's Education Minister (2019–2024). $GOTO was able to IPO in April 2022. Telkomsel's $450M (Rp 6.4T) into an unprofitable GoTo followed by a 82% stock plunge has spotlighted Nadiem's legacy. The AGO's March 2023 memo, revived in November 2025, alleges "unlawful actions" without governance, including IDX rule tweaks enabling GoTo's IPO. Nadiem wasn't directly involved post-2019, but public calls ( labor federation urging AGO probe) implicate him via GoTo's board ties to elites.

This funding supported GoTo's expansion into ride-hailing, e-commerce, and digital payments, but the company's persistent unprofitability (losses since 2010) and a sharp stock decline have raised red flags. The AGO's March 2023 memo flagged "unlawful actions" in the deal, citing governance failures and potential state losses exceeding Rp 4.5 trillion.

The investment's core suspicion is familial ties Boy Thohir (GoTo commissioner/shareholder) and Erick Thohir (SOE Minister overseeing Telkom). Erick's role enabling the deal despite risks. Tempo reports elite control over state bodies exacerbated issues. This mirrors Nadiem's alleged Google favoritism, suggesting a pattern of cronyism in Indonesia's tech-BUMN nexus.

The Indonesian state-owned company (BUMN) that invested in GoTo (the merged entity of Gojek and Tokopedia, founded by Nadiem Makarim) is PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM), through its subsidiary Telkomsel. It is estimated that Telkomsel invested more than $450m from 2020-2021 or even higher amount undisclosed prior. Meaning the indonesian people money is down 75-80% or $350m unrealized losses. 

The 2021 IDX decision  waived profit requirements for GoTo's listing, suspected of "significant intervention." As minister, Nadiem's influence on digital policy indirectly aided the process. DPR's 2022 probe flagged similar overvaluation fears

=> $GOTO wouldnt exist without Nadiem. 

The intense rivalry between Gojek (now part of GoTo, ticker $GOTO) and Grab ($GRAB) in Southeast Asia's ride-hailing, food delivery, FinTech, B2B AI  SuperApp markets escalated significantly from around 2018 onward, when Gojek began expanding aggressively beyond its Indonesian stronghold into territories where Grab was already dominant.

Gojek, founded in 2009 as a motorcycle taxi service in Indonesia, announced a major international push in May 2018 with a $500 million investment to enter Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, and the Philippines. This marked the start of direct head-to-head competition with Grab, which had built a strong regional presence (starting in Malaysia in 2012 and expanding across 8 countries by then).

~September 2018: Launch in Vietnam (a key Grab stronghold).
~November 2018: Entry into Singapore, Grab's home market and one of its most profitable.
~Expansions into Thailand and the Philippines followed, with Gojek using local teams and acquisitions (majority stake in Philippines' Coins in January 2019) to replicate its multi-service model.

This shift turned the rivalry from mostly Indonesia-focused to a full regional battle, as both companies aimed to become "super-apps" offering ride-hailing, food delivery, payments, and more.

2. Alternative if GOTO/GOJEK didnt get the funding from corrupted Nadiem. 

$GOTO would likely have remained a much smaller player in Indonesia, and most of us wouldnt know or hear about this company. It would probably go bankrupt in 2019-2020. 

Without the extra capital momentum (Google investments helped fuel growth and merger with Tokopedia in 2021 to form GoTo),Telkomsel(stated owned)  GoTo might have faced earlier funding constraints, reduced subsidies, slower super-app development, and potentially exited more markets sooner.

I did a few hypothetical projections, and it averaged out to be 90-95% market share today. 
~Registed drivers would be 10m+ drivers
~Revenue would be $9-$10B depending today
~Positive FCF and operating leverage would start in Q1/Q2 2021. 
~It would have gone IPO directly on Nasdaq instead of SPAC and gotten higher funding. GRAB Raised roughly $4.5B in Cash through SPAC merger with Altimeter Growth Corp or @altcap involved. 
~Valuation would be around $50B-$80B MC or $12.5-$20 or roughly 5-8 P/S, still a significant domestic US stocks.
~The Revenue growth will probably be around 35-40% from $9B-$10B base 2025.
~Grab, facing less competition, could have consolidated faster, raised prices earlier, and achieved higher margins/market share regionally.

3. Connecting the Dots

We can't deny Nadiem and investors of $GOTO ambition to be the SEA SuperApp, in a similar position like $GRAB today. However, it was funded by corruption, relaxed IPO, stealing money from poor children and Google chrome money drama. Despite all of that, there were thousands of articles spamming $GRAB to acquire $GOTO since 2020(Covid). So Nadiem already knew he was not going to win GRAB. The additional funding had serious consequences for everyone in the region. It hurt merchants, drivers, investors from both companies and especially the Indonesian people got nothing but social unrest, unfair pays. This was one of the major bear cases for all companies operating in this SuperApp idea, where analysts concluded NO MOAT, just whoever offered cheaper price. 

Then Alex Hungate joined $GRAB in Jan 2024 as COO, Grab SuperApp completely pivoted to a $AMZN $COST type of business model, where management focus only on customers, not trying to be the lowest price in the region. Alex has extensive background on Finance, Logistic, and operational effciency. Both @AnthonyPY_Tan and @alexhungate understood it was unsustainable to lowest price after lowest price to compete with corrupted $GOTO. The company focuses more on treating Merchants/Drivers like customers just like Users of the App. SuperApp went from few millions to 48m Monthly Transacting Users today. GRAB does not use active users, because it could go up to 200m members, they chose transparency for investors to see. Transacting users are where consumers paid for the services they needed. 

Analysts projected GRAB to grow only 12-14% in the next 3-5 years from 2023, yet the average growth is 35% or 3 times the analysts projection with corrupted $GOTO. $GOTO would probably go away in 2-3 years servicing its debt, it is probably the best thing to sell Mobility/Delivery to $GRAB for $1.5B and pay off the debt. $GOTO recently also got clapped by Indonesia regulators  in Jan 2026 where they can't collect 0.3-0.4% a day interest for its Fin Arm or 146% interest a year, this is worse than loan shark. 

Loan sharks were reported in the 70-100% a year which is ridiculous already. Now $GOTO Fin arm can only collect 0.1% interest rate per day. This is Interest per day, not per month, and still is 36.5% a year, which is higher than most US credit card companies btw. I understand many would argue the 146% interest rate is capitalism to price in risk. But I can assure you, 146% is peak stupidity and NOT Capitalism. And this will also make $GOTO Finarm much less profitable, 146% vs 36.5% interest. This is maximum pressure and leverage from Indo govt to put an end to $GOTO Mobility/Delivery Price War. 

This is why $GRAB is building its own Grab FICO system, where they would build payment/spending/repayment behavior on the app for its Merchants/Drivers/Users, the only way to price in risk to lend in the region where 60-80% are underbanked or 0 bank. 

Here's the direct comments from Alex:
"We are, in many ways, a data science company. We are learning every single second of every single day from how our models ingest all of the different data points that we can generate through our ecosystem. Unlike banks, we can access a lot of unconventional markers of likelihood to repay that allow us to underwrite segments of the population in Southeast Asia that currently cannot access credit. These are often known as underbanked, unbanked. A lot of what we do is about financial inclusion, bringing people into the market, allowing them to actually establish a credit record. About one-third of our customers could not access credit because they weren't on a credit bureau prior to borrowing from Grab and our financial subsidiaries. This is very important to us and very much aligned with our mission. The repayment record actually from those customers is very pleasing.

They know that when they repay us, they start to establish a credit record and they start to therefore become included in the financial and economic prosperity of Southeast Asia. We're very pleased to learn more about those customers and to bring them into the financial services domain for the first time. The credit models, every time we launch a new product, the credit models obviously take time to be established. What you're seeing this quarter is that across the banks and GrabFin, we're starting to see that we've got credit models maturing. We've got new models being launched all the time. We're increasing the cycle speed with which our data science improves these models. That's why going into this fourth quarter, if you run the numbers, we're predicting an acceleration of the loan book size. We also are indicating that that acceleration will continue into 2026"

4. What is the point of this thread?

I can't offer Financial Advice, and I prefer to hold my position in Shares with no option. In the recent rally, Many asked why I didnt initiate large option position, because I knew short sellers are still around, and the sell pressure from "Dumb money" was explosive or roughly 1.1B shares were sold from "Dumb money" to "Smart money". I knew it is not going to be easy ride especially short sellers are putting roughly $1B to short this small company. 

It is because of Nadiem/Goto/Gojek, Short sellers, bearish Analysts, and emotional retail investors base(from 40% now down to 16-18%); investors today can buy $GRAB at a massive discount. And Yes institutional onwership went from 56-57% to ~84% now. 

Current Cash Liquidity is $7.4B and $4.4B in equity investment with GrabFin is projected to be profitable in Q2/Q3 2026. Meaning all the core segments (Delivery/Mobility/Fin) are going to be profitable in H2 2026. Adjusted FCF is going to be $1B or higher TTM from Q3 2026, AKA a massive Cash Cow with monster Cash Position. 

In simple words, at $19.82B MC. 
$1 invested = $0.60-$0.70 of it are Cash, Equity, and FCF generation. Meaning, it could break even in absolute term by 2026-2027. 

And that is why Institutional onwership went to ~84%. @BlackRock,@GoldmanSachs,@Citi,@UBS,@jpmorgan,@MorganStanley, D. E. Shaw & Co,  Bridgewater, TCW Group, Howard Marks Oaktree and many more funds from EU are seeing massive growth potential and investment opportunities in economies within Southest Asia and other emerging markets mentions of Indonesia, India, Cambodia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. 

Conclusion: $GRAB would be $12.5-$20 a share without Nadiem years of corruption. Investors would not be able to buy $GRAB at discount like today or 2023-2025. Retail investors base would be higher in the 35-40% instead of 16-18%. But we are at the end of consolidation or GRAB at 90-95% market share. The goal is to growth MTUs to 350-400m and GrabUnlimited to 200-250m paid members. 

At $4.99 a month, that is less than 1% of monthly household income, and GRAB is just getting started with 6.5% penetration in the 700m population SEA. After consolidation, shareholders should expect expansion to new regions. The "Bottom of Pyramid" was just a significant socioeconomic and business theory/concept, but $GRAB just proved it is working. The only company that achieved positive operating leverage servicing folks at the bottom or the world's poorest consumers, yet much higher margin than $UBER and many other US companies. 

When a company turned a theory/concept into a reality, that is when most investors should be excited. Unfortunately, "Dumb money" turned emotional, and where "Smart Money" swallowed the float. Sadly, this is going to build wealth for "Smart money" and a small base of "Retail investor". I want retail investors to win, but I can't offer Financial Advice. 

I can only share what I learn about the business. And I tend to focus on DDs on companies I own along with $PLTR $AMD $TSLA $XYZ $HIMS and many others.

High conviction cannot be convinced, it has to be earned through countless hours of DDs. 

Alright, that is it. 

If you enjoy this kind of thread, slap the like/repost/bookmark to please the X Algo.

If you want to support my work further, consider subscribe to see more in-depth analysis. 

Not Financial Advice!

BREAKING $GRAB & $GOTO Update 👀

TLDR: It seems the Indonesian prosecutors are aligned with my months of analysis on this matter. That $GOTO wouldn't exist or get to IPO without Nadiem. Then We wouldn't have 5-6 years of price war and billions in losses for both companies, and especially the impact on Merchants and Drivers in many countries in SEA.

The article from https://t.co/RuuyoQoenR details the prosecutors' indictment against Nadiem Anwar Makarim in his ongoing corruption trial at the Jakarta Corruption Court. This is part of the high-profile case involving alleged corruption in the procurement of Chromebook laptops and Chrome Device Management (CDM) services for Indonesia's education digitalization program (2019–2022) under the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology (Kemendikbudristek), where Nadiem served as minister.

Prosecutors stated Nadiem abused his authority:
~Directing procurement specifications toward Chrome OS and Chrome Education Upgrade (Google products) via Ministerial Regulations No. 11/2020 and No. 5/2021.
~Making Google the sole provider of the digital education ecosystem (via Google Workspace for Education).
~Ignoring prior failed attempts (2018 procurement), real educational needs (especially in remote/3T areas), proper planning, evaluation, and pricing references (via e-Katalog or SIPLah).
~Prioritizing the project despite mismatches with actual requirements, leading to misuse of state budget (APBN).

This allegedly caused state losses of around Rp 2.18 trillion (=USD $130–$140 million), broken down as:
~Rp 1.56 trillion from overpriced or unnecessary Chromebook procurement.
~Rp 621 billion from unnecessary CDM services.

Prosecutors also stated:
Nadiem is accused of receiving Rp 809.596 billion (≈ Rp 809.59 billion or roughly US$50–55 million) in illicit benefits. Prosecutors link this to an investment from Google into PT Aplikasi Karya Anak Bangsa (PT AKAB) — a GoTo-related entity — via PT Gojek Indonesia. They state that much of PT AKAB's funding came from Google's total investment of US$786.999 million (≈ US$787 million). This is tied to Nadiem's 2022 LHKPN (wealth report), which showed securities worth Rp 5.59 trillion, with his overall wealth peaking at around Rp 4.8 trillion that year.

Google investment in $GOTO is approximately $787m

~Prosecutors allege that most funds flowing into PT Aplikasi Karya Anak Bangsa (PT AKAB) — the pre-merger parent entity of Gojek (which became part of GoTo after the 2021 merger) — came from Google's total investment of around US$787 million.

~They highlight a specific top-up or additional investment of about US$59 million from Google into PT AKAB around 2020–2021, coinciding with key ministerial decisions favoring Google Chromebooks in Indonesia's education procurement.

Google (Alphabet) participated in multiple funding rounds for Gojek (pre-merger) and the combined GoTo group, primarily in the pre-IPO phase leading up to GoTo's April 2022 listing:

~Google was part of a major pre-IPO fundraising round in November 2021, where GoTo raised over US$1.3 billion from various investors (including Google, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Fidelity, Temasek, Tencent, and others). Google's specific portion in this round isn't publicly broken out in detail beyond the trial references.

~Earlier investments trace back to Gojek rounds (e.g., Google invested in Gojek as early as 2018 alongside Temasek and others in a $1.2 billion round, with Google's stake estimated around $100 million at times).

~Separate smaller investments exist, like Google's  1.6% stake in Tokopedia (pre-merger) valued at about $1.1 million in 2020 reports, but these are minor compared to the Gojek/GoTo focus.

Source:https://t.co/yeC8l5tqRK
